Hi Alec / Priya — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can kick the vendor security assessment forward: 

- Redwood takeaways: SignalBridge is evaluating us for question-answer and enrichment workflows (low PHI footprint per your notes) with an initial pilot for two internal teams.
- Key compliance items we discussed to confirm before we start the SIG/CAIQ prefill: SOC 2 status (Type I/II and most recent audit date), whether you process PHI or plan to in pilot (HIPAA scope), and any EU data residency/GDPR concerns.

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you confirm SOC 2 status and provide the latest attestation (or report if available)?
2) Please confirm whether SignalBridge will route any PHI to Redwood in the pilot. If yes, we'll need a BAA conversation.
3) If you prefer, we can send our SIG prefill template to populate; otherwise we can initiate the standard CAIQ.
4) Target timeline: if we can get prefill within 7 business days we can start evidence collection and aim for an internal security review within 3 weeks.

I'm attaching the REDWOOD prefill spreadsheet to make things quicker (one tab for SOC2/ISO, one for network controls). If you want us to tailor the scope (SOC2-only vs. SOC2+HIPAA), tell us which option you prefer and we'll adjust the evidence asks.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call to walk through the prefill.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Hi Stephanie — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying points from our side before we start filling anything out: 

1) SOC 2: We have a SOC 2 Type II report (most recent period ended 2026-06-30). We can provide the attestation under NDA.
2) PHI / HIPAA: For the pilot we do not plan to route PHI to a vendor; our ingestion will be metadata and redacted customer notes. That said, SignalBridge handles PHI for a small subset of customers in production and we need to confirm segregation measures.
3) Data residency: Primary infra is in us-east-1. Some customers have EU tenancy; we use strict tenant isolation but do not currently replicate production data to EU. If Redwood requires EU processing or an EU data residency guarantee, we need to discuss routing.

Can you confirm whether Redwood needs the SOC 2 report itself or a SOC 2 Type II summary + control mapping? Also share any preferred evidence format for the BAA (if later required).

I've attached a short SignalBridge security overview for context (no sensitive attachments). We'll try to get the SOC 2 under NDA by end of this week.

Thanks — Priya

Thanks Priya — super helpful. A few clarifications from our side and how we typically proceed so you can pick the least friction path: 

- SOC 2 artifacts: a scanned SOC 2 Type II report under NDA is ideal; failing that a control mapping (CSV/Excel) that shows the coverage plus the auditor name/date also works for initial review.
- For pilot scope where you confirmed no PHI is routed, we will not require a BAA up-front. If production use later involves PHI, we will reopen BAA discussions.
- Data residency: for most evaluations we accept us-east-1 tenancy as long as there is a documented isolation model. If EU residency becomes a hard requirement, we have options (dedicated region routing) but that changes procurement timelines.

Attached is a prefilled SIG/CAIQ starter sheet (redwood-sig-prefill-template.xlsx) with the fields we typically own to speed evidence collection. If you can return the spreadsheet with the sections your team can fill, we'll only ask for targeted attachments (e.g., SOC2 PDF, network diagrams, IdP config screenshots).

Suggested evidence asks (starter):
- SOC 2 Type II PDF (or control mapping)
- List of subservice vendors + subprocessors (CSV)
- Network diagram or short description of tenant isolation
- Authentication/SSO screenshots (IdP metadata)
- Patch cadence and vuln scanning summary (one paragraph)

I'll upload the prefill to the vendor portal and share the Drive link here once done; please let us know if you want a short screen-share to walk the sheet. Target: collect prefill within 7 business days, internal security review within 3 weeks.

Best,
Stephanie
